data.narrative:
Pila Energy is a seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Cole Ashman that has raised $4M to date. The relevant comp universe consists of 9 private frontier-energy peers (including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen) and 1 public comparable (LNZA), though direct same-stage peers remain sparse.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable valuation lever. Using total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a typical 2.5x seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier yields an implied valuation of $10M. A peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient datapoints meeting narrow filter criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comps within Climate & Energy all fell below the three-company threshold needed for statistical reliability).

The analysis supports a triangulated range of $8M to $12M, with a median point of $10M. This valuation rests on a single methodological input—stage-progression mechanics—which limits confidence. Key uncertainties include the absence of tight peer comparables at seed stage, the early maturity of frontier-energy venture capital pricing, and the specific technology positioning of Pila within a heterogeneous sector. A narrower range would require either traction data (revenue, unit economics, technology validation) or access to recent seed-stage rounds in the direct peer set.
